score.verdict: Your site is likely invisible or poorly represented in most AI search answers.

components.label: Direct Answers: 35/100
components.detail: The content contains some definitional statements about Notion's features, but these are marketing-oriented rather than informational. Phrases like 'Q&A agents Answers questions instantly using knowledge you already have' and 'Enterprise Search One search for everything' provide brief feature descriptions, but lack substantive explanations of what these features actually do, how they work, or what problems they solve in concrete terms. The content prioritizes persuasive language over educational content. Example: "'Q&A agents Answers questions instantly using knowledge you already have' — states what it does but not how it works, what knowledge sources it connects to, or what 'instantly' means in practice."

components.label: Statistical Richness: 55/100
components.detail: The page contains 8 statistics, which is moderately high density for a short page. However, most statistics are about market position and user adoption ('Over 100M users worldwide', '62% of Fortune 100', '#1 knowledge base 3 years running') rather than performance metrics or research-backed claims about effectiveness. The statistics are also repeated multiple times, inflating the count. Only one statistic hints at concrete outcomes: 'Streamlined workflows to reduce timelines by 3x' — but this lacks context about what workflows or how this was measured. Example: "'Over 100M users worldwide' and '62% of Fortune 100' — impressive adoption metrics, but no source cited and no methodology explained. The '3x' timeline reduction claim appears without supporting evidence."

components.label: Citation Quality: 5/100
components.detail: The content almost entirely lacks citations. The only attribution present is '(G2)' next to three '#1' rankings, but this is minimal — no specific report dates, methodology, or links to verify claims. Customer quotes are unattributed beyond company names implied by context. No links to research, case studies, or third-party validation. The '3x' productivity claim has zero supporting evidence. Example: "'#1 knowledge base 3 years running (G2)' — provides award source but no report date, category definition, or link to verify. Contrast with: no citation at all for 'Streamlined workflows to reduce timelines by 3x'."

components.label: Structure Clarity: 40/100
components.detail: The page has 11 H2 headings suggesting attempted organization, but the actual content structure is fragmented and repetitive. The extracted text shows clear repetition of entire sections ('Over 100M users worldwide' block appears 3 times identically). Headings are often vague ('Keep work moving 24/7', 'Bring all your work together') rather than descriptive. The flow jumps between features, testimonials, and statistics without clear thematic grouping. No table of contents or clear hierarchy for scanning. Example: "The statistics block beginning 'Over 100M users worldwide' is repeated verbatim three times in the content, indicating either carousel content or poor content management that creates noise rather than structure."

components.label: Conversational Match: 25/100
components.detail: The language is highly marketing-optimized rather than conversationally aligned with how users actually ask questions. Phrases like 'Think together', 'Keep work moving 24/7', and 'Less tracking. More progress.' are taglines, not answers. The content doesn't match query patterns like 'What is Notion used for?', 'How does Notion AI work?', or 'Notion vs competitors' — instead it assumes visitor intent is already to purchase. Feature descriptions use imperative/command language ('Capture context, find answers') rather than explanatory language. Example: "'The AI workspace that works for you' — tagline that doesn't answer any specific question. Compare to missing content like 'Notion is a collaboration platform that combines documents, databases, and AI assistance' which would match 'What is Notion?' queries."

components.label: No structured data (JSON-LD) on homepage
components.detail: No <script type='application/ld+json'> blocks found on the homepage. This is the single biggest missed opportunity for AI visibility — schema.org data tells AI engines exactly what your page is about.

findings.title: No structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) on homepage
findings.evidence: No <script type='application/ld+json'> tags were found in the page HTML.
findings.should_be: At minimum, Organization and WebSite schema should be present.
findings.fix:
Add this to your homepage <head> (replace the placeholders):

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Your Business Name",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "logo": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "description": "One sentence describing what your business does.",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/yourhandle",
    "https://www.linkedin.com/company/yourcompany",
    "https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/yourcompany"
  ]
}
</script>

Tip: if you use WordPress, plugins like Yoast SEO or RankMath can generate this automatically. If you use Webflow, it's under Page Settings > Schema Markup.

findings.title: Canonical URL points to a different domain
findings.evidence: Canonical tag points to "https://www.notion.com/" but the page is served from a different domain. This tells search engines the "real" version lives elsewhere.
findings.should_be: Canonical should point to the page's own URL (self-referencing).
findings.fix:
Change the canonical to point to this page's own URL:

<link rel="canonical" href="https://notion.so/">
